reason: This passage (Nehemiah 5) critiques the oppressive exercise of hierarchical power by nobles and rulers who exploit the common people through debt and land seizure. Nehemiah, though positioned at the top of the hierarchy as governor, deliberately uses his authority to challenge and restrain oppressive hierarchical practices. He rebukes the nobles, refuses to exploit his office's privileges (not eating the governor's bread), and advocates for restoring equity to those below. The text presents justice, compassion, and fear of God as more important than the strict exercise of hierarchical authority. While hierarchy itself is not eliminated, the passage clearly discourages its strict or exploitative application.
